items.title: Paraguay seizes major digital bank tied to president, leaving millions of customers in limbo
items.description: Paraguay’s central bank seized a major digital lender with close ties to President Santiago Peña, throwing the savings of millions of customers into limbo.
items.content: <media:description type="plain"><![CDATA[The headquarters of Ueno bank, a major digital lender stands in Asuncion, Paraguay, after the nation's Central Bank seized it due to its solvency ratio, Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. items._ogDesc: Paraguay’s central bank seized a major digital lender with close ties to President Santiago Peña, throwing the savings of millions of customers into limbo.
items.body:
ASUNCIÓN, Paraguay — Paraguay’s central bank seized a major digital lender with close ties to president Santiago Peña early Tuesday, throwing the savings of millions of customers and hundreds of millions of dollars in public funds into limbo.

The central bank’s board voted unanimously Monday to put Ueno Bank into resolution after its solvency ratio — a measure of a bank’s capital against its risk-weighted assets — fell below half the legal minimum, the regulator said.

Later Tuesday, central bank president Carlos Carvallo, who ran the lender before Peña appointed him to the post, said he had signed his resignation letter but would stay on for now to oversee the takeover. “The central bank needs calm to do its job,” he said.

  • Latest updates on international news here

Unlike bankruptcy proceedings in court, resolution allows regulators to transfer a failing bank’s deposits to more stable banks before its remaining assets are liquidated to repay creditors.

Ueno says it has about three million customers, equivalent to roughly 60 per cent of the adult population of the South American country, and manages US$800 million to US$850 million in public money. That includes about US$380 million invested by Paraguay’s state pension and health fund, known as IPS, according to the fund.

Customers said they were locked out of their accounts on the bank’s app. Police stood guard outside branches in what officials described as a precaution against unrest.

Carvallo’s appointment to the central bank was controversial from the start

The intervention marks a dramatic turn in a scandal that has shadowed Peña since he took office in 2023. Soon after his inauguration, he named Carvallo to lead the central bank, a move critics denounced as a conflict of interest. The central bank has said Carvallo recused himself from decisions involving Ueno.

Peña remained a business partner of Grupo Vázquez, the conglomerate that owns Ueno, until March 2025, though the bank says he was never a shareholder or investor. He repeatedly brushed off concerns about the bank’s finances, accusing the media of stoking public fear.

Meanwhile, government agencies and state funds poured money into Ueno, the leading Paraguayan newspaper ABC Color has reported, citing Finance Ministry records. Last month, Ueno’s president, Juan Manuel Gustale, said public money accounted for about a quarter of the bank’s deposits.

Peña’s office announced Monday that he had canceled a planned trip to an international summit in Spain, vaguely citing priorities at home.

The fallout has spread to his long-dominant conservative Colorado Party. Paraguay’s presidents are limited to a single term, and Peña’s Vice President Pedro Alliana had been seeking the party’s nomination for the 2028 election. On Monday, Alliana said he was putting his bid on hold, citing the “financial crisis” surrounding Ueno.

“If we don’t get our house in order, there’s no presidential project,” he told local radio.

The central bank says it will launch an investigation

The central bank said the intervention would allow it to wind down Ueno while protecting customers’ savings and preventing disruption to other banks. It insisted the problems were confined to Ueno, saying the situation “does not affect the financial system as a whole.”

Carvallo told reporters that regulators first raised concerns about Ueno’s loans to companies tied to its owners. Banks face strict limits on such lending because it allows owners to steer customers’ money into their own businesses.

A deeper inspection uncovered more serious irregularities, which the central bank plans to report to the authorities, he said. He also blamed recent news reports about the bank’s troubles for accelerating its collapse.

The central bank said it would appoint officials to take over the bank from its management, determine what it is worth and protect its assets. It also plans to investigate who was responsible for the bank’s decline and impose sanctions.

  • Latest updates on currencies here

Each depositor is guaranteed up to 228 million Paraguayan guaraníes, or about US$38,000, from a central bank fund, the regulator said. Under Paraguay’s banking law, that money must be paid within 15 days, a deadline that can be extended once by another 15.

About 97 per cent of Ueno’s depositors have balances fully covered by the guarantee, according to preliminary estimates cited by central bank board member Marco Aurelio González. For amounts above that limit, the central bank stopped short of promising full repayment, saying only that it would seek “the greatest possible protection.”

Whether those depositors recover money above the guarantee will depend on the outcome of the resolution process and a possible liquidation, said Gladys Vera, the state pension fund’s finance manager.

Vera told local media that retirees would be paid as usual this month because the money for monthly payments is held at another bank. She said the fund would take legal action to try to recover its investment and would find another bank for the 32,000 retirees who collect their pensions through Ueno.

Jorge Saenz And Isabel Debre, The Associated Press

DeBre reported from Buenos Aires, Argentina.

items.body:
DuPont lifted its full-year profit forecasts on Tuesday and projected current-quarter earnings above Wall Street estimates after a third-quarter performance boost from strong healthcare, aerospace and industrial water markets demand.

Shares of the industrial materials maker rose 7.6 per cent in morning trading.

The global chemicals industry has been grappling with persistent overcapacity and uneven demand in key end markets.

DuPont, however, has benefited from capital deployment initiatives including the spinoff of its electronics business, debt reduction and share repurchases as well as price increases to offset higher feedstock and energy costs.

  • Latest updates on company news here

Its third-quarter results showed it was able to offset higher costs through price increases while expanding margins, Morningstar analyst Seth Goldstein said, and the market is reacting to management’s strong outlook.

The company raised its 2026 adjusted core profit outlook to nearly $1.79 billion from its previous forecast range of $1.75 billion-$1.77 billion.

It expects annual adjusted earnings of $7.47-$7.52 per share, compared with $7.17-$7.32 per share previously.

DuPont expected full-year results to come in at or above the high end of its prior guidance, CFO Antonella Franzen said.

It concluded a $250 million accelerated share repurchase program and substantially completed $100 million of open-market share repurchases during the third quarter, DuPont said.

  • Latest updates on international news here

The company plans to repurchase an additional $250 million of shares in the fourth quarter.

The pace of future share buybacks would depend on the timing of potential mergers and acquisitions, DuPont executives said in an earnings call.

Net sales at its healthcare and water technologies segment rose nearly 4 per cent to $865 million from a year earlier, while sales at its diversified industrials segment increased 4.2 per cent to more than $1 billion.

Large water projects in the Middle East are now expected to be pushed into 2027 due to ongoing disruptions, company executives said.

Wilmington, Delaware-based DuPont forecast fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of $1.90-$1.95 per share, above analysts’ average estimate of $1.87 apiece, according to data compiled by LSEG.

It reported adjusted profit of $2.09 per share for the third quarter, topping analysts’ estimate of $1.87 per share.

(Reporting by Pooja Menon in Bengaluru; Editing by Pooja Desai)

items.body:
Yum Brands said same-store sales at Taco Bell were recovering after a wider-than-expected decline in the third quarter following a multistate cyclosporiasis outbreak that hurt traffic at the Tex-Mex chain.

Taco Bell has been offering value deals such as its combo boxes to attract inflation-hit consumers in the United States. Executives said on a post-earnings call that such deals were helping attract lower-income households.

The business was first linked to the outbreak in early July, causing a 20 per cent drop in weekly foot traffic at its outlets at the peak of the epidemic, according to Placer.ai.

U.S. health authorities declared the outbreak was over last month.

  • Latest updates on company news here

Yum said loyalty-program promotions and partnerships were helping it bring back customers, and added that Taco Bell’s same-store sales have risen about 1 per cent so far this quarter.

“(Customers are) actually spending 5 per cent more and visiting 6 per cent more frequently than the consumers we lost,” CEO Chris Turner said.

Recovery in the business has been more pronounced among younger consumers, Consumer Edge analyst Michael Gunther said.

Shares of the company, which completed the divestiture of its Pizza Hut chain in September, pared premarket gains and were flat in morning trading.

Taco Bell’s same-store sales fell 4 per cent in the reported quarter, its first decline in about six years, missing analysts’ expectations for a 0.9 per cent drop, according to data compiled by LSEG.

A focus on value also helped Burger King parent Restaurant Brands International QSR.N beat sales expectations last week. Bigger rival McDonald’s MCD.N is set to report quarterly results on Wednesday.

Overall Yum same-store sales were flat from a year earlier, below estimates for 0.9 per cent growth. KFC same-store sales rose 1 per cent, missing expectations for a 2.1 per cent increase.

Yum’s adjusted profit per share fell 1.3 per cent to $1.56, but beat estimates of $1.49.

(Reporting by Neil J Kanatt in Bengaluru and Waylon Cunningham in New York; Editing by Shinjini Ganguli)

items.title: Apple drops with most of Wall Street, but gains for other Big Tech stocks cushion the blow
items.description: The U.S. stock market is drifting in mixed trading on Tuesday, with Apple falling but other Big Tech stocks picking up the slack following their own big swings.

items._ogDesc: The U.S. stock market is drifting in mixed trading on Tuesday, with Apple falling but other Big Tech stocks picking up the slack following their own big swings.
items.body:
NEW YORK — The U.S. stock market is drifting in mixed trading on Tuesday, with Apple falling but other Big Tech stocks picking up the slack following their own big swings.

The S&P 500 added 0.2 per cent in early trading, even though more stocks fell within the index than rose. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 232 points, or 0.4 per cent, as of 9:35 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was 0.5 per cent higher.

  • S&P 500 market updates here

The stock market has been shaky recently as technology and artificial-intelligence stocks have swung on worries their prices shot too high in the frenzy around AI. Several of the most influential AI-related stocks held up better on Tuesday, which supported the market, though they flipped from gains in the morning to losses in the afternoon a day earlier.

Nvidia rose 3.1 per cent and was the strongest force pushing upward on the S&P 500 Tuesday. CoreWeave rose 2.6 per cent. The company that’s borrowed money to buy AI chips that it rents out to customers over the cloud has been at the center of the industry’s swings recently.

Apple was long seen on Wall Street as a Big Tech company that’s less dependent on AI. But it’s still feeling the effects of the AI boom.

Memory chips for computers have become more expensive because of the demand created by the rush to build AI data centers. Those additional expenses are hitting Apple, which said it expects to make less profit from each $1 of its revenue during the final three months of this year.

That helped send Apple’s stock down 3.4 per cent, even though the seller of iPhones and Mac computers reported stronger profit and revenue for the latest quarter than analysts expected.

  • Latest technology news on BNNBloomberg.ca

Palantir Technologies fell 4.2 per cent even though it likewise reported a better profit than expected. The software company said it made more money from working with U.S. companies than from the U.S. government for the first time, as U.S. commercial revenue soared 148 per cent from a year earlier.

Tuesday’s midterm elections may also be keeping financial markets unsteady, but history suggests that they may not matter much for the broad market. Going back to 1970, the S&P 500 has had a positive return in the six months following a midterm election every time, according to Brock Weimer, an analyst at Edward Jones.

Some on Wall Street worry that a Democratic sweep of Congress this time around could lead to more regulations and restrictions on AI development. But Donald Trump would still be president and have the power to veto. And Wall Street generally prefers split control of Washington, which it sees as offering less risk of transformative policies that could reshape the economy.

On the winning side of Wall Street Tuesday were stocks of several companies that reported stronger profits for the summer than analysts expected.

Celanese climbed 4.9 per cent, and DuPont added 7 per cent.

Expectations are high for all kinds of companies to continue to deliver big gains in profits as the U.S. economy keeps chugging along, even with high inflation and elevated interest rates. That helped send the S&P 500 to a record high last month.

In the oil market, prices continued to swing. Brent climbed above $107 per barrel in the morning before briefly dropping below $101 on continued uncertainty about what will happen in the war with Iran. It was most recently down 0.9 per cent at $103.80.

In stock markets abroad, indexes were mixed across Europe and Asia. South Korea’s Kospi dropped 3.6 per cent for one of the world’s sharpest moves following losses for its two tech giants, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.

Stocks rose 0.3 per cent in Australia after the country’s central bank raised its benchmark interest rate for the fifth time this year.

AP Writers Elaine Lai, David McHugh and Rod McGuirk contributed to this report.

items.body:
Marathon Petroleum on Tuesday beat Wall Street estimates for third-quarter profit on stronger refining margins and struck a US$4.2 billion deal to sell two refineries and related midstream assets to Carl Icahn-controlled CVR Energy.

Marathon’s shares rose about 2 per cent in premarket trading.

The Iran war has disrupted oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz, while attacks on energy infrastructure across the Middle East and Russia have tightened fuel supplies, pushing up refined product prices relative to crude.

The resulting surge in refining margins has boosted refinery profitability, creating an attractive opportunity for Marathon to monetize assets and for CVR to expand its operations.

  • Stay on top of your portfolio with real-time data, historical charts and the latest news on oil

Marathon’s quarterly refining and marketing margin more than doubled to $45.70 per barrel.

The company’s crude capacity utilization was 100 per cent, with throughput of 3.2 million barrels per day (bpd), compared with 95 per cent utilization and 3 million bpd a year earlier.

For the fourth quarter, Marathon expects total refinery throughput of 3.08 million bpd.

The top US refiner earned $26.93 per share on an adjusted basis, topping analysts’ estimates of $24.47, according to LSEG.

Marathon returned $3.3 billion to shareholders during the quarter, raised its quarterly dividend by 10 per cent and increased its share buyback capacity to $8.1 billion with an additional $5 billion authorization.

DIVESTITURE PLANS

Marathon will receive $3.45 billion for the St. Paul Park refinery in Minnesota and the Mandan refinery in North Dakota, while its midstream subsidiary, MPLX MPLX.N, will receive $750 million for related infrastructure.

The refineries have a combined crude processing capacity of 177,000 bpd.

Marathon plans to reinvest its proceeds primarily along the US Gulf Coast, while MPLX will deploy its share toward growth projects in the Permian and Marcellus basins.

Commodities trader Trafigura has agreed to invest $800 million in newly issued CVR shares for a minority stake.

Trafigura will also become the exclusive crude supplier and trading intermediary for the acquired refineries and enter into petroleum product offtake arrangements.

The deal is expected to close by the end of 2026.

(Reporting by Sumit Saha and Arunima Kumar in Bengaluru; Editing by Maju Samuel)

items.title: Organigram to Acquire Aurora and Establish a Global Cannabis Leader
items.description: Organigram Global Inc. and Aurora Cannabis Inc. announced that they have entered into an arrangement agreement.
items._ogDesc: Organigram Global Inc. and Aurora Cannabis Inc. announced that they have entered into an arrangement agreement.
items.body:
This press release is provided by Business Wire and is published as received.

TORONTO & EDMONTON, Alberta--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Organigram Global Inc. (NASDAQ: OGI) (TSX: OGI) (“Organigram”) and Aurora Cannabis Inc. (NASDAQ: ACB) (TSX: ACB) (“Aurora”) today announced that they have entered into an arrangement agreement (the “Arrangement Agreement”) pursuant to which Organigram will acquire all of the issued and outstanding common shares (the “Aurora Shares”) of Aurora at a price of C$7.80 per Aurora Common Share (the “Transaction”).

The Transaction values Aurora at approximately C$561 million on a fully diluted equity value basis. The consideration represents a 93% premium to the unaffected closing share price of Aurora Shares on the TSX as of August 10, 2026, the last full trading day of Aurora prior to the announcement by Curaleaf Holdings, Inc. (“Curaleaf”) of its intention to launch a hostile takeover bid for Aurora (the “Unaffected Price”), and a 21% premium relative to the current bid value of the Curaleaf hostile offer3 (the “Hostile Bid”) as most recently amended on October 6, 2026, which was unanimously rejected by Aurora’s Board of Directors.

The Transaction provides Aurora shareholders with compelling immediate value, meaningful choice in how they receive their consideration, and the opportunity for continued participation in the future growth and value creation of the combined company.

Together, Organigram and Aurora will create a global cannabis champion with a leadership position in Canada, Europe and Australia and a growing presence across other key regions. The two Canadian-headquartered cannabis companies will boast a global platform with greater scale, broader capabilities, financial strength and international reach. Organigram’s recreational cannabis leadership, production network, R&D platform and European medical commercial operations complement Aurora’s global medical cannabis leadership, established international presence, and EU-GMP certified manufacturing capabilities. The combined company will also benefit from the support of Organigram’s cornerstone strategic shareholder, BT DE Investments Inc., a wholly-owned indirect subsidiary of British American Tobacco (“BAT”), a global consumer goods company with demonstrable innovation, marketing and product development capabilities around the world.

“This Transaction is a defining step in Organigram’s strategy to build a disciplined, global cannabis leader,” said James Yamanaka, CEO of Organigram. “By bringing together Aurora’s established global medical cannabis platform with our Canadian operations and growing international footprint, we are creating a larger, stronger, and more diversified company. We are excited to build on our complementary operations, expertise, capital resources, and cultures to accelerate growth, meet the growing global demand, and drive long-term profitable growth.”

“Combining with Organigram will accelerate Aurora’s international growth strategy by strengthening commercial execution, expanding our product and R&D capabilities, and extending our global operating network,” said Miguel Martin, Executive Chairman and CEO of Aurora. “For Aurora’s shareholders, the Transaction is the result of a robust strategic review process and delivers compelling value today, meaningful choice in how they receive it and the opportunity to participate in the future of a leading cannabis company.”

Compelling Strategic and Financial Rationale

Under the terms of the Arrangement Agreement, Aurora shareholders will have the option to elect to receive:

The Transaction will be carried out by way of a court-approved plan of arrangement under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) and is subject to the following approvals:

The issuance of Organigram Shares pursuant to the Transaction and Private Placement (defined below) is subject to the approval by a simple majority of votes cast by Organigram shareholders at a special meeting of Organigram shareholders, excluding votes held by BAT, as required under MI 61-101 and the rules of the TSX.

Details of the Transaction and the required shareholder votes will be included in a joint information circular that Organigram and Aurora expect to mail to their respective shareholders in due course. The special meetings for Organigram shareholders and Aurora shareholders are expected to be held in December 2026.

BAT, which is entitled to cast 30% of the votes attaching to Organigram Shares, has entered into an irrevocable voting agreement agreeing to vote its Organigram Shares in favour of the Transaction and against any competing acquisition proposals. The voting agreement with BAT will not be terminable until six months following termination of the Arrangement Agreement in certain circumstances. In addition, each of the other directors and officers of each of Aurora and Organigram have entered into customary voting agreements agreeing to vote their Aurora Shares or Organigram Shares in favour of the Transaction. The voting and support agreements with directors and officers will terminate automatically upon termination of the Arrangement Agreement.

In addition to the shareholder approvals, the Transaction will be subject to regulatory approvals, as well as the approval of the Supreme Court of British Columbia. Subject to the satisfaction of such conditions, the Transaction is expected to be completed in January 2027.

The Transaction would be structured to provide a tax-deferred rollover to eligible Canadian-resident Aurora shareholders who receive Organigram Shares, subject to applicable law and advice from their own tax advisors.

BAT Concurrent Private Placement / Financing

In connection with financing the Transaction and concurrently with the closing of the Transaction, BAT will acquire, on a private placement basis (the “Private Placement”), 141.0 million Organigram Shares at a price of C$1.33 per share for gross proceeds of £0.70926 (or C$1.33 based on the GBP/CAD exchange rate on November 2, 2026) million for total gross proceeds of £100,000,000 (or C$187.5 million based on the GBP/CAD exchange rate on November 2, 2026) (the “Private Placement Proceeds”) pursuant to the terms of a subscription agreement dated November 2, 2026 (the “Subscription Agreement”). To the extent BAT’s ownership of Organigram Shares in Organigram exceeds 30.0% of the total issued and outstanding Organigram Shares on a post-issuance basis (the “30% Threshold”), BAT would, in lieu of Organigram Shares, be issued non-voting Class A convertible preferred shares of Organigram (the “Preferred Shares”). The Private Placement Proceeds will be used to finance the cash portion of the Consideration and certain related transaction expenses of Organigram. The Preferred Shares are eligible for conversion into Organigram Shares in accordance with their terms, provided that such conversion would not result in ownership by BAT or its affiliates, associates, related parties and any joint actors exceeding 30.0% of the total issued and outstanding Organigram Shares on a post-conversion basis.

ATB Financial Senior Secured Credit Facilities

ATB Financial (“ATB”) has provided a fully committed and underwritten commitment for senior secured credit facilities of up to $210 million (the “Loan Facilities”). The Loan Facilities will be established by amending and restating Organigram’s existing $70 million senior secured credit agreement with ATB. ATB alone is providing the full commitment, as lead arranger and sole bookrunner. ATB’s commitment is not conditional on syndication. ATB may syndicate a portion of the Loan Facilities to other lenders, who may become party to the credit agreement from time to time. ATB will also act as administrative agent for the Loan Facilities.

The Loan Facilities include:

The amended and restated Loan Facilities will be available on the Closing Date. Availability is subject only to a limited set of conditions precedent, customary for acquisition financings on a “certain funds” basis. These include completion of the acquisition substantially at the same time as funding, receipt of the final order approving the arrangement, receipt of the committed equity proceeds, and the accuracy of certain specified representations. The Loan Facilities will mature three years after closing and bear interest at ATB’s applicable benchmark rates plus an applicable margin based on the ratio of net funded debt to EBITDA. The Loan Facilities will be subject to customary financial covenants, including a maximum net funded debt to EBITDA ratio and a fixed charge coverage ratio.

Superior Alternative for Aurora Shareholders to the Hostile Bid

The Transaction emerged from a robust strategic review process conducted by Aurora, under the oversight of a committee of independent directors (the “Aurora Special Committee”), advised by independent legal and financial advisors. The review process involved an extensive market check, including outreach to multiple parties, in connection with the unanimous rejection of the Hostile Bid, as detailed in the Notice of Change to Aurora’s Directors’ Circular dated October 14, 2026. The Aurora Special Committee and the Board of Directors of Aurora (the “Aurora Board”) believe that the Transaction is superior to the Hostile Bid and the best actionable path forward to maximize value for Aurora shareholders.

The Aurora Special Committee and the Aurora Board continue to reiterate that the Hostile Bid is not in the best interests of Aurora or its shareholders and unanimously recommend that shareholders REJECT the Hostile Bid by taking no action and DO NOT TENDER their Aurora Shares to the Hostile Bid. Aurora intends to file a second Notice of Change to its Directors’ Circular confirming the Aurora Board’s continued recommendation to reject the Hostile Bid and vote in favour of the Transaction (the “Second Notice of Change”), which will be made available on Aurora’s SEDAR+ profile at www.sedarplus.ca and on EDGAR at www.sec.gov.

Aurora Shareholders who have already tendered their Aurora Shares to the Unsolicited Curaleaf Hostile Offer can withdraw their Aurora Shares by contacting their broker or Kingsdale Advisors by toll free phone call in North America to 1-800-749-9052, or call or text: 416-623-4172 or by email at contactus@kingsdaleadvisors.com.

Unanimous Board Approvals and Recommendations

The Transaction and the Private Placement were unanimously approved (with BAT’s nominees to the Board abstaining from the vote with respect to the Private Placement) by the Board of Directors of Organigram (the “Organigram Board”), after receiving a recommendation from the Investment Committee of the Organigram Board (the “Investment Committee”). The Investment Committee and the Organigram Board have unanimously determined that the Transaction and the Private Placement are in the best interests of Organigram.

In connection with Organigram’s review and consideration of the Transaction, BMO Capital Markets has provided an opinion to the Investment Committee and the Organigram Board to the effect that, as of the date of such opinion, and subject to the assumptions, limitations and qualifications to be set forth in its written opinion, the Consideration to be paid by Organigram pursuant to the Arrangement Agreement is fair, from a financial point of view, to Organigram.

The Transaction was unanimously approved by the Aurora Board, after receiving a unanimous recommendation from the Aurora Special Committee. The Special Committee and the Aurora Board determined that the Transaction is in the best interests of Aurora, and the Aurora Board is recommending that Aurora shareholders vote in favour of the Transaction.

In connection with Aurora’s review and consideration of the Transaction, Fort Capital and Origin Merchant Partners have each provided an opinion to the Aurora Special Committee and the Aurora Board to the effect that, as of the date of such opinion, and subject to the assumptions, limitations and qualifications to be set forth in its written opinion, the Consideration to be received by Aurora shareholders pursuant to the Arrangement Agreement is fair, from a financial point of view, to such shareholders.

A copy of the Arrangement Agreement and the joint information circular with respect to the Transaction will be filed on Organigram’s and Aurora’s respective SEDAR+ profiles and will be available for viewing at www.sedarplus.ca and filed or furnished to the Securities and Exchange Commission on EDGAR (see www.sec.gov).

Advisors and Counsel

BMO Capital Markets is serving as the financial advisor to Organigram in respect of the Transaction and has provided a fairness opinion to the Investment Committee and the Organigram Board. Goodmans LLP is serving as legal advisor to Organigram.

Fort Capital Partners is serving as financial advisor to Aurora in respect of the Transaction and has provided a fairness opinion. Origin Merchant Partners is serving as financial advisor to the Aurora Special Committee and has provided a fairness opinion. Legal counsel to the Aurora Special Committee is Torys LLP. Legal counsel to Aurora is Stikeman Elliott LLP and Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP.

Osler, Hoskin & Harcourt LLP is serving as legal counsel to BAT.

To learn more about the Organigram-Aurora Transaction, visit www.OrganigramXAurora.com and www.VoteYesAurora.com.

Organigram Global Inc. is listed on the NASDAQ Global Select Market and TSX. The Company’s wholly owned subsidiary, Organigram Inc., is a licensed cultivator and processor. Through its acquisition of Sanity Group GmbH (“Sanity Group”), Organigram participates in the German medical cannabis market and other emerging markets within Europe. Organigram is focused on producing high-quality cannabis for adult consumers, as well as extending the Company’s global footprint. Organigram has also developed and acquired a portfolio of cannabis brands, including Edison, Big Bag O’ Buds, SHRED, Monjour, Tremblant, Collective Project, Trailblazer, BOXHOT and DEBUNK. Through its acquisition of Sanity Group, Organigram’s European brands include Vayamed, avaay, ZOIKS, Endosane Pharmaceuticals, VAAY, and Grashaus Projects. Organigram operates facilities in Moncton, New Brunswick and Lac Supérieur, Quebec, with a dedicated edibles manufacturing facility in Winnipeg, Manitoba. The Company also operates two additional cannabis processing facilities in Southwestern Ontario; one in Aylmer and the other in London. The facility in Aylmer houses best-in-class extraction capabilities, and is optimized for formulation refinement, post-processing of minor cannabinoids, and infused pre-roll production. The facility in London will be optimized for labelling, packaging, and national fulfillment. The Company is regulated by Health Canada under the Cannabis Act and the Cannabis Regulations.

Aurora is a global leader in medical cannabis, dedicated to improving lives through scientific expertise, proven performance, and a deep commitment to patient care. items.title: Pfizer raises 2026 forecasts as Eliquis, cancer drugs drive Q3 results
items.description: Pfizer raised its full-year profit and revenue forecasts on Tuesday as strong demand for its recently acquired cancer drug Padcev and blockbuster blood thinner Eliquis led to higher-than-expected third-quarter results.

items._ogDesc: Pfizer raised its full-year profit and revenue forecasts on Tuesday as strong demand for its recently acquired cancer drug Padcev and blockbuster blood thinner Eliquis led to higher-than-expected third-quarter results.
items.body:
Pfizer raised its full-year profit and revenue forecasts on Tuesday as strong demand for its recently acquired cancer drug Padcev and blockbuster blood thinner Eliquis led to higher-than-expected third-quarter results.

Pfizer is now targeting annual sales of $62 billion to $64 billion, up from the prior forecast of $60.5 billion to $62.5 billion, and earnings of $2.95 to $3.05 per share, compared with its previous outlook of $2.80 to $3.00 a share.

CEO Albert Bourla said the raised outlook reflected the strong quarterly performance as well as confidence in the company’s strategy, pipeline and long-term growth prospects.

The New York-based drugmaker has spent billions of dollars on acquisitions and licensing deals to bolster its pipeline and reassure investors about its growth prospects despite looming patent expirations and declining sales of COVID-19 products that had generated a revenue windfall during the pandemic.

  • Latest updates on company news here

The company spent $43 billion in 2023 to acquire cancer drugmaker Seagen and $10 billion for obesity drug developer Metsera last year.

Pfizer’s acquired products are increasingly contributing, but the longer-term growth story still depends on the success of experimental treatments in the pipeline, Bernstein analyst Courtney Breen said.

Among the near-term catalysts investors are watching for are late-stage data for experimental cancer drug mevrometostat and early results from Metsera’s amylin-based obesity drug.

Pfizer said late-stage data for mevrometostat, previously expected by year-end, is now anticipated in the first quarter of 2027.

Pfizer shares were about flat in premarket trading.

NEW CFO

Separately, the drugmaker on Tuesday said it appointed Cecile Guegan as chief financial officer, effective November 1, succeeding Dave Denton, who left in August to take on a similar role with Nike NKE.N.

Guegan’s appointment provides “more perceived stability ahead of decisions on setting 2027 guidance,” said BMO Capital analyst Evan Seigerman.

Sales of blood thinner Eliquis, which Pfizer shares with Bristol Myers Squibb BMY.N, rose 25 per cent to $2.52 billion, above estimates of $2.46 billion, driven by higher net price in the US, the company said.

Pfizer and Bristol had cut the price of the blood clot preventer after it was selected as one of the first 10 medicines subject to Medicare price negotiations under the Inflation Reduction Act.

The price cut allowed them to avoid penalties imposed by the US government’s Medicare health insurance program for price increases that outpace inflation.

The company reported a third-quarter adjusted profit of 87 cents per share, topping analysts’ estimates by 14 cents, according to LSEG data.

Total revenue for the quarter came in at $16.58 billion, above Wall Street estimates of $15.87 billion.

(Reporting by Christy Santhosh and Mariam Sunny in Bengaluru, Michael Erman in New Jersey; Editing by Arun Koyyur and Bill Berkrot)

This press release is provided by GlobeNewswire and is published as received.

TORONTO, Nov. 03, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Today, Vencora – a global buy-and-hold-forever acquirer of banking, financial services, and insurance technology companies – announced the acquisition of CT InsureTech (CTI), formerly Charles Taylor InsureTech, a leading provider of insurance technology, software, and services to global insurers and brokers. With offices in London, Buenos Aires, and Mexico City, CTI combines decades of insurance knowledge with forward-thinking technology to provide software and deliver enterprise services to the global insurance market, shaped by a deep understanding of the complex realities of insurance and the genuine needs of the people working within it.

“Our focus at Vencora is on building enduring technology businesses that customers can rely on for decades. CT InsureTech is exactly the kind of high-quality, mission-critical platform Vencora is built for – with deep domain expertise, strong customer relationships, and a clear path for continued growth,” said Vencora CEO Kevin Bradley. “We are committed to supporting the business to enhance its products, develop its people, and help ensure customers continue to benefit from stable, innovative solutions.”

CTI will continue to serve existing and new customers through three distinct operating units, each with a clearly defined focus and target market:

CTI Insurance Modernization builds on nearly 40 years of insurance technology experience to help insurers, brokers, banks, and affinity partners unlock potential and capture sustainable value. Its adaptable platforms and services support insurance products across all lines of business, distribution, and operations, with capabilities in pricing, risk selection, and fraud detection. The unit enables clients to build on existing investments and expand their capabilities, with optional outsourcing services. CTI Insurance Modernization will continue to be overseen by Lautaro Mon.

CTI Digital Transformation specializes in the implementation of core insurance platforms, supporting insurers through complex, end-to-end transformation programs. Its services encompass core system implementation, legacy system migration, data transformation, and cloud migration, enabling insurers to transition to modern, scalable, and API-driven platforms. CTI and Vencora look forward to deepening their partnership with Fadata, an important strategic partner to the Digital Transformation business, and working closely together to support customers undertaking complex core platform and digital transformation programs. CTI Digital Transformation will be overseen by Gonzalo Geijo.

CTI London Market & Managed Services provides solutions designed for participants in the London Market – including bordereaux management, document and process management, delegated authorities control, and claims process optimization – and managed services including end-to-end outsourced technology, enhanced customer experience, and risk management and compliance. CTI London Market & Managed Services will continue to be overseen by Kieran Maloney.

“I am excited about the addition of CT InsureTech to the Vencora portfolio of companies,” said Nathan Partington, Portfolio Manager for Vencora. “As the dedicated platform for insurance software and services within Constellation Software, Vencora is uniquely qualified to support CTI’s continued success and future growth. We are confident that Vencora is the right permanent home for CTI’s employees, customers, and products, and we look forward to continuing to expand Vencora’s presence in the United Kingdom, Europe, and Latin America.”

Vencora acquires mission-critical software businesses serving banking, financial services, and insurance customers and holds them forever. Vencora is an independent portfolio within Volaris Group, an operating group of Constellation Software. Vencora offers its businesses a community that understands their industry, customers, regulatory environment, product challenges, and the pressure of building software financial institutions rely on every day.

items.title: Apple shares slide as Ternus sounds alarm on memory costs
items.description: Apple shares fell about 4 per cent in premarket trading on Tuesday after the tech giant warned that rising memory costs would squeeze gross margins, stoking investor concerns over persistent supply-chain uncertainties and mounting AI expenses.
items.content: <media:description type="plain"><![CDATA[The Apple logo is illuminated at a store in Munich, Germany, April 2, 2026. (AP Photo/Matthias Schrader, File)]]></media:description><media:credit role="author" scheme="urn:ebu">Matthias Schrader</media:credit>
items._ogDesc: Apple shares fell about 4 per cent in premarket trading on Tuesday after the tech giant warned that rising memory costs would squeeze gross margins, stoking investor concerns over persistent supply-chain uncertainties and mounting AI expenses.
items.body:
Apple shares tumbled about 4 per cent on Tuesday as its first results under new CEO John Ternus showed that rising memory chip costs were denting the iPhone maker’s envied margins, the latest sign of the AI boom’s toll on the technology industry.

Sales of smartphones, PCs and other electronics have already suffered this year from price hikes driven by soaring memory chip costs as the AI industry’s data-center race absorbs supply.

That even Apple, long known for its supply-chain prowess, is feeling the squeeze shows virtually no firm is spared. The warning follows Intel’s bleak forecast last week on collapsing PC chip demand.

“What we’re seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented,” Ternus said on his first earnings call as CEO.

“For the December quarter, we expect even higher memory costs. And looking beyond the December quarter, we see the pricing for memory purchases continuing to increase.”

  • Latest technology news on BNNBloomberg.ca

Gross margin, the share of revenue Apple keeps after production costs, slipped to 47.9 per cent in the September quarter from the June quarter, even with the boost from tariff refunds.

The company expects its gross margin to shrink further to between 45 per cent and 46 per cent in the December quarter, as it also grapples with the costs of rolling out an AI-powered Siri that is central to its AI plans.

To cushion the blow, Apple has been drawing on memory chips bought earlier at lower prices and has moved to lock in supplies.

Its manufacturing purchase obligations, or orders placed with suppliers and contract manufacturers, increased by $33 billion to $89.7 billion as of Sept. 26, a filing showed.

TERNUS’ PRODUCT BLITZ

Apple’s drop on Tuesday also weighed on the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq. Expectations were high going into the results because Apple’s restraint on AI spending had made it a refuge for investors uneasy about the AI boom’s soaring costs, helping its shares gain by more than a fifth so far this year.

The memory crunch comes just as Ternus rolls out a product blitz packed with Apple firsts, including its first foldable phone, iPhone Duo, and its first touchscreen MacBooks.

Apple has also been raising prices to cushion the hit to profitability. That, along with strong demand for the premium iPhone 18 Pro lineup, helped it beat fourth-quarter sales estimates and forecast upbeat revenue.

But some analysts warn that more price hikes risk scaring off buyers as inflation is already climbing.

The CEO comments imply “Apple products are going to become even more expensive, which is not ideal at a time when the consumer is feeling the pinch from a higher cost of living,” said Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell.

Apple is set to lose over $170 billion in market value from its $4.94 trillion valuation, if losses hold.

The stock trades at nearly 35 times expected earnings over the next 12 months, compared with 18.23 times for Alphabet GOOGL.O and 23.43 times for Microsoft MSFT.O.

(Reporting by Harshita Mary Varghese in Bengaluru; Editing by Devika Syamnath)

TORONTO — U.S. asset manager Blackstone and four Canadian institutional investors have signed a US$3.1-billion deal to acquire a non-controlling stake in the Mitsubishi Corp. subsidiary that holds an interest in LNG Canada, the country’s first liquefied natural gas export facility. 

The investor group includes the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, the Ontario Municipal Employees Retirement System, the Investment Management Corp. of Ontario and the Public Sector Pension Investment Board. Blackstone and the funds are together acquiring a 49.9 per cent interest in the Mitsubishi unit. 

“LNG Canada is a high-quality, globally strategic asset with strong long-term fundamentals and attractive return potential for the CPP fund,” Geoff Souter, managing director at CPP Investments, said in a news release Monday.

Rick Campbell, senior managing director at Blackstone Credit & Insurance, called LNG Canada “one of Canada’s most significant energy projects,” adding it will “help meet rising energy demands across global markets.” New York-based Blackstone manages US$140 billion through its infrastructure and asset-based credit platform. 

  • Latest updates on investing here

LNG Canada is a joint venture between Shell, PetroChina, Malaysia’s Petronas, Japan’s Mitsubishi Corp. and South Korea’s KOGAS.

Mitsubishi holds a 15 per cent interest through its subsidiary. It will retain its full share of the plant’s LNG supply. 

In September, LNG Canada announced it will go ahead with the Phase 2 expansion project at its liquefied natural gas export terminal in Kitimat, B.C. The expansion will double LNG Canada’s capacity to 28 million tonnes a year. The expansion has been referred to the federal major projects office, which aims to speed up infrastructure deemed in Canada’s national interest. 

Richard Brooks, climate finance director at environmental group Stand.earth, said Canadians should be “extremely alarmed” to see pension funds investing in LNG on behalf of millions of workers and retirees. 

“Canadians should have a say where and with whom their retirement funds are invested. While geopolitical instability has driven up interest in Canadian LNG, this is still not a risk-free investment, particularly in the long term,” Brooks said in a news release. 

  • Latest economic news on BNNBloomberg.ca

He said the world is scaling up clean energy infrastructure in order to reduce dependence on energy imports. The price of energy has skyrocketed in Europe and Asia since the U.S. and Israel launched their war on Iran in February, disrupting supplies from the Persian Gulf. 

“The bottom line is that every dollar of workers’ pensions put into LNG Canada is a dollar not building the clean energy future. That capital should instead be accelerating clean energy projects with better long-term returns,” said Brooks. 

Adam Scott, director of Shift Action for Pension Wealth and Planet Health, said the pension funds have broken trust with their members. 

“We’re now using our taxes and our retirement savings against us to harm our climate,” he said in a news release. “It’s deeply irresponsible and indefensible.”

Blackstone has provided $150-million in financial backing to another natural gas export project in the works on the West Coast, Ksi Lisims LNG near the Alaska border, through its affiliate Blackstone Energy Transition Partners.

Lauren Krugel, The Canadian Press

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 2, 2026.

items.description:

The post Canadian Banks Brace For Mortgage Losses, 3x Pre-Pandemic Share appeared first on Better Dwelling.
items._ogDesc: Canadian banks see more losses from delinquent mortgages in their future—a lot more losses. Mortgage loss expectations have 3x since 2019.
items.body:
Canada’s banks are bracing themselves for the fallout from the real estate bubble. Last week, the CMHC warned that the share of mortgages in arrears will climb further—especially in Ontario. The banks seem to agree, as the data shows they’ve been preparing for a sharp increase in mortgage losses. The median allowance for mortgage losses has more than doubled over the past four years.

Canadian Banks Expect Mortgage Losses To Climb Sharply

Ratio of expected credit losses to total residential mortgage balances.

Source: CMHC; Better Dwelling.

Lenders need to be prepared for losses on bad loans. It doesn’t matter how much borrowers are vetted; the reality is some won’t be fully repaid. To account for this, lenders record an allowance for credit losses—an estimate of the money they do not expect to recover. It reflects expected losses, not just losses that have already occurred. Those expectations have risen sharply.

The CMHC compared each bank’s mortgage portfolio against its allowance for credit losses. The median—half of banks are better, half are worse—had an allowance equivalent to $149 per $100,000 in mortgages in Q2 2026, up 13.2% from a year earlier. That share has climbed 138.1% over the past 4 years, more than doubling. It has roughly tripled (+202.8%) since Q2 2019, back in the before times.

Keep in mind that these measure expected losses relative to mortgage balances. The banks are preparing for higher losses on each dollar lent, and they’ve lent a lot more dollars over that period. Their expectations of losses have grown alongside their mortgage portfolio over the past 7 years.

Canadian Mortgage Losses Expected To Rise Further At Some Banks

The median bank’s increase is sharp, but it hides a much sharper climb at some banks. The 75th percentile, the threshold for the top 25% of banks, saw allowances reach $337 per $100,000 in mortgages, up 47.9% from last year. The share is more than double (+126%) the median, and the highest in the data going back to 2015.

Canadian Mortgage Loss Expectations Grew At 3 In 4 Banks

Most banks expect higher mortgage losses, with roughly 3 in 4 reporting higher allowances than a year earlier. That share was just 53% a year prior, an already tenfold increase from the 5% recorded in Q2 2022. The share of banks reporting higher expected losses has gone from only 1 in 20 banks to 3 in 4 over just four years.

While the amount remains small relative to total mortgage debt, the increase is hard to ignore. Banks are preparing to lose more of each dollar lent, and more lenders expect losses to grow. That also only captures part of the rising pressure, with distress rising even faster among mortgage investment entities (MIEs).

items.title: As hopes of a Canada-US deal rise, here’s what’s at stake for housing
items.description: Positive remarks by Prime Minister Carney and President Trump have fuelled talk of a deal, potentially brightening the mortgage outlook
items.content: <p>Positive remarks by Prime Minister Carney and President Trump have fuelled talk of a deal, potentially brightening the mortgage outlook</p><img src="https://cdn-res.keymedia.com/cms/images/us/074/0373_639292419264737498.png" alt="" style="max-width:240px" />
items._ogDesc: Positive remarks by Prime Minister Carney and President Trump have fuelled talk of a deal, potentially brightening the mortgage outlook
items.body:
Formal talks between Canada and the US on a resolution to the tariff war could begin soon after prime minister Mark Carney’s Sunday social media post describing a productive recent discussion on the issue with US president Donald Trump.

Trade tensions have weighed against Canada’s economic outlook since the beginning of last year and emerged as a significant factor in the housing market’s continued malaise, pushing plenty of potential homebuyers to the sidelines and damaging consumer confidence.

While discussions between US and Canadian negotiators have yet to resume, a positive resolution to the trade war could have big implications for the national housing market.

Prospects for a 2027 recovery, some mortgage professionals say, could hinge massively on whether tariff tensions ease.

And Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation (CMHC) has highlighted how the trade war is worsening the mortgage strain for many borrowers in tariff-impacted parts of the country such as Southern Ontario, which has borne the brunt of US levies on steel, aluminum, automotive vehicles and parts, and agricultural products.

With homebuilding also taking a hit, the national housing agency’s deputy chief economist Aled ab Iorwerth (pictured top) told Canadian Mortgage Professional a swift end to the trade war could potentially improve the currently dire construction outlook.

“I’m a little bit concerned on the housing supply situation that higher interest rates are affecting developers,” he said. “Now on that side, if the situation were resolved, then maybe developers would have a lot more confidence in home construction.

“From a long-term affordability [perspective], that would be positive. I think if the overall uncertainty lowered… it would give renewed confidence to people who want to go out and buy a home. If you knew the dispute was over, I think that greater certainty would help the overall economy.”

Leaders’ comments suggest potential relief for borrowers ahead

Last week, Trump told a rally in Michigan that the trade war could be settled “pretty soon,” as he stepped up campaigning ahead of the crucial midterm elections, set to take place on November 3.

Trump and Carney’s recent statements mark the first hint of a possible détente since an end to tariff negotiations in August triggered a sudden escalation in the trade war.   

Ab Iorwerth said the ongoing trade war is part of the reason mortgage strain seems worse in Southern Ontario than other parts of the country, even though there’s no sign of a wider mortgage meltdown caused by rising arrears.

“There’s a lot of protection within the system so I don’t think we’re looking at a systemic issue, but there’s a lot of people being adversely impacted by what’s happening to them individually,” he said. “And I think a lot of households are facing challenges with these higher interest rates that they’re bearing and the uncertainty over the trajectory of mortgage rates.

“There’s still that lingering concern over inflation and then there’s uncertainty on the macroeconomic front with trade. So I think all of this is creating a lot of stress for individual households about what might happen.”

Iran and inflation add further complications for housing

While tariffs were the defining story of 2025 for the Canadian economy, they’ve been joined this year by surging fuel prices because of the war in Iran – another curveball that could complicate the picture even if the trade war ends.

Those higher fuel prices have sparked fears of a wider spillover into headline inflation, one of the main reasons the Bank of Canada opted to hike its benchmark interest rate last week for the first time in over three years.

Against that backdrop, the central bank doesn’t see the housing market bouncing back in 2027 – although it underlined the positive effects an end to the trade war could potentially have.

A Canada-US deal reducing tariffs “would increase exports and business investment, boosting employment and incomes,” the BoC said in its latest Monetary Policy Report. “Higher demand could increase the pass-through from higher energy prices. The removal of counter-tariffs would provide an offset.”

items.description: Haventree’s COO talks lending trends and the ever-evolving Canadian borrower
items.content: <p>Haventree’s COO talks lending trends and the ever-evolving Canadian borrower</p><img src="https://cdn-res.keymedia.com/cms/images/us/074/0270_639292444699523088.jpg" alt="" style="max-width:240px" />
items._ogDesc: Haventree’s COO talks lending trends and the ever-evolving Canadian borrower
items.body:
The alternative lending space is changing – and as the big banks continue tightening their lending criteria, alt lenders are seeing their market share grow. At MortgageFest, we caught up with Haventree Bank chief operating officer Joe Cote to hear his thoughts on current trends and what’s in store for the sector down the line.

[00:00] There's not a very simple straightforward borrower type anymore. We're talking about great credit scores that are well into the 700s, low 800s, but we're talking about life happens. Brokers are small business owners. This affordability issue has now compounded for 5 years and the alternative space is going to be, I think, a huge eye-opener for a lot of the brokers.

[00:30] Fergal McAlinden: All right. So, next up we have Joe Cote, Chief Operating Officer at HipBilt Bank, whose booth we see just over here. Have you been having many productive conversations with brokers today?

[00:40] Joe Cote: Lots of discussions. I certainly think that there's been a lot of changes throughout the industry, specifically with HipBilt, which is very exciting. And having a lot of brokers come back and are interested to see, you know, tell me more. Tell me what you're doing. We're hearing a lot of exciting things that have been happening over the course of the last 6 to 12 months. Tell me what's happening over the course of the next 6 to 12 months and how can we partner together?

[01:00] Fergal McAlinden: For sure. And the event is happening at a really interesting time for the industry. I mean, not that we haven't had any non-eventful times over the past few years. It's just been one thing after the next. But 2026, how are you assessing the market this year? How's it been?

[01:13] Joe Cote: I think obviously the market has had a fairly large impact on a lot of brokers and a lot of lenders, the community at large. We are still very happy and fortunate with our position and our performance so far this year. We've got great partners. I think that value proposition that we have certainly been working on has been what, the proof in the pudding of being able to look to those partners. We've got a lot of partners that have come back. I think that they're very excited with the service, the products, and the relationships that we've built. And from an overall performance standpoint, we're going to finish the year actually fairly strong and we got some good growth prospects for 2027.

[01:45] Fergal McAlinden: I was interested to hear, Joe, from lenders about borrower types. We know that they've evolved a lot over the past few years. I'm wondering if there's a specific type of borrower that you feel best placed to cater to in the current market.

[01:57] Joe Cote: I think the short answer to that is there's not a very simple straightforward borrower type anymore. Well, I think one of the opportunities has certainly been around the evolution of the alt space and how it's very much part of the prime offering now. And it used to be around bruised credit, which is still very much the case and will always be part of the ideal client profile that the alt space was built off of.

[02:18] But now we look at the tightening credit box from a lot of the larger Schedule 1 banks. That business flow, as it's been tightening, has actually been coming into the alternative space. And that's not necessarily a bad thing. We're talking about great credit scores that are well into the 700s, low 800s. But we're talking about life happens. We're talking about divorces. We're talking about CRA. Multiple properties, business for self.

[02:43] It doesn't necessarily mean bruised credit anymore. It just means maybe not as simple from a credit profile standpoint. So, we are truly running the entire gamut of what I would say is the alternative space is now alt A through to what was bruised credit before. And I'd love to see the evolution of the space and the value that we're bringing back to the Canadian consumers.

[03:04] Fergal McAlinden: For sure. And I think that evolution, nobody's expecting that to slow anytime soon, especially with how the market is this year and some of the challenges being faced by buyers. When it comes to brokers, how have you been dealing with them this year? Are there any kind of approaches you've been keeping in mind with brokers?

[03:19] Joe Cote: Yeah, a big emphasis of our partnership model with brokers has been, how do we just focus on building our processes, our expectations, our interaction models completely around the broker community. And thinking about brokers as small business owners.

[03:34] I've been saying this a lot just recently on stage. I think the biggest thing was around brokers are small business owners. It is all about the experience. It's about the referral business. And if they land a great client experience based on the partnership that they have with the lender, that client's going to come back. They're going to refer more business.

[03:52] And that alternative space, again, especially in the small business community and or gig economy, we've got so many borrowers that are looking for solutions that they didn't even know existed before. So, we've basically repositioned, I would say, a lot of our processes and policies to be built around brokers and the client experience, keeping that really at heart.

[04:10] Fergal McAlinden: Great stuff. Looking ahead, 2027, hard as it is to believe, is just around the corner. Any trends that you're keeping an eye on or anything that you're expecting to be a big factor next year?

[04:20] Joe Cote: It's too fast. I miss summer already. I would say the trend, if anything, is probably going to be continuing. If you think about it, a couple of things. One has been the compounding effect of the interest rate environment, the tariffs, both in terms of just cost of goods as well as taxation on it, especially for small business owners.

[04:40] All those financing needs actually aren't going away. The financing needs are going to increase, especially if you think about this affordability issue has now compounded for 5 years. That's taxing a lot of Canadians, and that problem's not going to get any easier in the current environment.

[04:56] Not only what's happening with Canada and the US, but certainly I think in terms of the interest rate environment over the course of the next 12 months, there's not a single person that's expecting interest rates to stay flat. In that increasing environment, it's going to only compound the problem, and brokers are going to need to understand that business model.

[05:15] They're going to need to find ways to actually support their clients who are going to have needs, and knowing full well that the traditional means of prime sourcing is not necessarily going to be as viable as it used to be historically. And the alternative space is going to be, I think, a huge eye-opener for a lot of the brokers that are not currently accessing the alt space like they should be.

[05:27] Fergal McAlinden: For sure, and on that rate question, as you mentioned, I think we're all just strapped in waiting to see what happens on the bond market and on trade war and everything.

[05:34] Joe Cote: Yeah.

[05:34] Fergal McAlinden: Yeah, the only thing that's certain is that we have more uncertainty ahead, I think, is the way to put it. Maybe just one last word on the event, Joe. Have you met your target audience, and we'll be seeing you next year?

[05:43] Joe Cote: Absolutely. It's been wonderful, actually. Not only have I met, from an audience perspective, everybody in terms of our partners, as well as potential net new partners, both in terms of brokers, as well as a lot of other broker ancillary partners here.

[05:58] I think about the technology providers, I think about net new products that are coming on the market. I can point to a couple over there, which I just think are phenomenal in terms of the innovation that is showcased at the event, and I love being part of it, hearing the stories, how we can better service our clients.

[06:12] And looking at these partner solutions on how we can kind of improve the experience, I will definitely be back.

[06:15] Fergal McAlinden: Love to hear it. Okay, great stuff. Thank you for stopping by. Much appreciated. Then enjoy the rest of the event.

[06:19] Joe Cote: Thanks for having me.

items.title: Ontario credit unions lift profits as 90-day loan arrears climb
items.description: Early mortgage delinquency eased in Q2, but regulator data shows deeper arrears quietly building
items.content: <p>Early mortgage delinquency eased in Q2, but regulator data shows deeper arrears quietly building</p><img src="https://cdn-res.keymedia.com/cms/images/us/074/0388_639292407563693929.png" alt="" style="max-width:240px" />
items._ogDesc: Early mortgage delinquency eased in Q2, but regulator data shows deeper arrears quietly building
items.body:
Ontario credit unions grew assets and posted sharply stronger year-over-year profits in the second quarter of 2026, even as deeper loan arrears kept building, according to the latest Sector Outlook Report from the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario (FSRA).

Sector assets across the 48 institutions reached $106.47 billion at June 30, up 4.24% year over year.

Return on average assets (ROAA), the regulator’s core profitability measure, rose to 46 basis points from 30, as deposit costs fell faster than loan income.

One basis point equals 0.01%.

Credit union mortgage delinquency eases, but deeper arrears build

Residential mortgages remain the sector’s anchor. Credit unions held $57.92 billion in home loans at quarter-end, up 2.68% year over year, while commercial lending rose 1.97% to $27.44 billion.

The share of residential mortgages more than 30 days past due slipped to 1.13% from 1.15% in the first quarter, helping total 30-day delinquency record its first quarterly decline since the third quarter of 2024.

Year over year, though, mortgage delinquency was up 21 basis points, and commercial delinquency jumped 98 basis points to 2.80%.

The report’s tables point to strain further down the pipeline.

Loans more than 90 days delinquent rose to 1.08% of the total book from 0.99% in the first quarter and 0.71% a year earlier, while loan-loss allowances jumped 37.2% to $399 million.

Five of the 48 credit unions posted negative returns.

That mirrors the wider province, where Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation (CMHC) expects Ontario mortgage arrears to keep worsening until mid-2027.

CMHC deputy chief economist Aled ab Iorwerth flagged the regional split in an October interview on trade-driven rate volatility and arrears.

“We’re watching arrears and delinquencies very closely. They’re particularly acute in Toronto, less so in Vancouver,” ab Iorwerth said.

“It’s just that they’re going up quite rapidly and it’s a source of concern. Maybe I should extend it beyond Toronto to include southern Ontario as well – but then you have places like Alberta where the economy remains strong and arrears and delinquencies remain contained.”

Jessica Rickerby, President of CMBA-ON, and Aled ab Iorwerth, Deputy Chief Economist at CMHC, warn that rising interest rates could further challenge housing affordability and prolong mortgage renewal pressures for Canadian borrowers. https://t.co/9P0c7D7qBi — Canadian Mortgage Professional Magazine (@CMPmagazine) November 2, 2026

What does the FSRA outlook mean for broker files?

The quarter predates tighter policy: the Bank of Canada held at 2.25% through June, then raised its rate to 2.50% on October 28.

Credit unions enter that shift with liquidity up 45 basis points to 12.88% and borrowings down 25.25%.

Lenders in the broker channel are already sharpening scrutiny. Jamie Doolittle, head of BMO BrokerEdge, spoke on a MortgageFest Canada panel on prime lending in September.

“We are very focused on making sure that the story and the documentation and the numbers align,” she said.

“Having those conversations upfront and telling that clear and concise story is going to allow underwriters to make a decision faster.”

FSRA said it issued the first edition of its Enhanced Data Collection Supplemental Report in September, with the next edition expected in the first quarter of 2027.

items.title: FSRA bars Ontario mortgage agent after Tribunal finds dishonesty
items.description: Alongside the licence refusal, FSRA imposed $15,000 in administrative penalties
items.content: <p>Alongside the licence refusal, FSRA imposed $15,000 in administrative penalties</p><img src="https://cdn-res.keymedia.com/cms/images/us/074/0388_639292393193875248.png" alt="" style="max-width:240px" />
items._ogDesc: Alongside the licence refusal, FSRA imposed $15,000 in administrative penalties
items.body:
Ontario’s mortgage industry watchdog has barred a former mortgage agent from the province’s broker market after a regulatory tribunal found him responsible for three separate contraventions, including allowing himself to be used to facilitate dishonesty.

The Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario (FSRA) has refused to renew the licence of Raouf Ghadrdoust, who held a Level 1 mortgage agent licence from July 1, 2008, until March 31, 2023.

Alongside the licence refusal, FSRA imposed $15,000 in administrative penalties, following an order signed on October 14, by Troy Harrison, Acting Director of Litigation and Enforcement, by delegated authority from FSRA’s chief executive officer.

The Financial Services Tribunal held an electronic hearing across three days in June, concluding that Ghadrdoust had contravened the Mortgage Brokerages, Lenders and Administrators Act, 2006 (MBLAA).

Its Reasons for Decision, dated October 1, directed FSRA’s chief executive to implement the proposed penalties and licence refusal in full.

Three violations behind the decision

The Tribunal identified three distinct contraventions. Ghadrdoust was found to have dealt in mortgages for remuneration outside his licensed brokerage, in breach of section 2(3) of the MBLAA.

He also received remuneration from a person other than his registered brokerage, contrary to section 4(1) of Ontario Regulation 187/08.

The third and most serious finding was that he allowed himself to be used to facilitate dishonesty, in violation of section 3.1 of the same regulation.

Ghadrdoust applied to renew his licence on March 24, 2023. A Notice of Proposal to refuse that renewal was issued on September 3, 2024, with the resulting Tribunal hearing upholding the regulator’s position in its entirety.

Under the October order, Ghadrdoust must pay the $15,000 penalty within 30 days, or the debt becomes enforceable as an order of the Superior Court of Justice.

Brokers weigh in on rising enforcement standards

The case arrives as FSRA has sharply escalated its enforcement posture across Ontario’s mortgage sector.

The regulator’s first-ever annual enforcement report, released earlier this year amid a broader surge in mortgage industry penalties, revealed that mortgage-related sanctions in 2025 totalled approximately $860,000 – a roughly 50% increase over the prior year.

Two of the three contraventions – dealing outside a licensed brokerage and accepting fees from a non-registered party – mirror the provisions at the centre of FSRA’s February action against former agent Shan Jamal.

He received $20,000 in penalties for arranging multiple off-book mortgage deals and routing payments through other entities to avoid detection.

The “facilitating dishonesty” finding under section 3.1 of Ontario Regulation 187/08 has also appeared in a significantly larger case: FSRA fined former agent Lin Liang $275,000 after she brokered 15 deals connected to an alleged fraud scheme, with the Tribunal finding she ought to have known she was being used to facilitate dishonesty, the same standard applied against Ghadrdoust.

For many established brokers, the trajectory is long overdue. Joe Sammut, broker of record at Mortgage Architects – A Better Way in Ontario, told Canadian Mortgage Professional the crackdown marked a meaningful shift in how the regulator views the profession.

“I’ve seen more cases against bad actors in the last 12 to 18 months than in previous years,” Sammut said.

“They seem to be clamping down and cleaning up, and they’re making sure the fines they’re enacting on people are publicized.”

Carmen Costa, principal broker and owner at TCG Lending Centres in Ontario, echoed the view that tougher oversight ultimately serves the industry’s best interests.

“Mortgage brokers deal with complex products that can have long-term financial consequences for consumers, so strong oversight is important,” she told CMP in an interview on Ontario’s regulatory landscape.

items.description: OREA praised Ontario’s housing measures – but one extension could determine who truly benefits
items.content: <p>OREA praised Ontario’s housing measures – but one extension could determine who truly benefits</p><img src="https://cdn-res.keymedia.com/cms/images/us/074/0388_639292266160812841.png" alt="" style="max-width:240px" />
items._ogDesc: OREA praised Ontario’s housing measures – but one extension could determine who truly benefits
items.body:
The Ontario Real Estate Association (OREA) has welcomed Ontario’s 2026 Fall Economic Statement, tabled by Finance Minister Peter Bethlenfalvy on October 29. But the association is pressing the Ford government to extend its new-home harmonised sales tax (HST) relief beyond March 2027, warning the current deadline limits how many buyers can benefit.

Acting Chief Executive Officer Diane J. Brisebois, speaking for OREA’s nearly 100,000 REALTOR Members across the province, credited the Ford government for advancing both the $8.8-billion Canada-Ontario Partnership to Build and temporary HST relief on new homes valued up to $1 million, two measures OREA has long advocated for.

“These types of bold actions, including their promise to continue funding and supporting municipalities that already do not levy development charges, will have a positive effect within many parts of our economy,” Brisebois said.

“It will help expand critical infrastructure, enable more housing supply to hit the market, lower the cost of homes, and create good-paying jobs.”

What Ontario’s 2026 fall economic statement delivered

Tabled against a projected $16.9-billion deficit, up from $13.8 billion in the March 2026 budget, the statement reaffirmed several key housing and economic measures.

Chief among them for the mortgage industry: the 10-year, $8.8-billion Canada-Ontario Partnership to Build, designed to fund housing-enabling infrastructure and reduce municipal development charges, and temporary HST relief on new homes valued up to $1 million, providing up to $130,000 in savings per eligible transaction.

The statement also confirmed an $8.7-billion Canada-Ontario action plan to shield Ontario’s industrial base from ongoing US tariff pressures.

Statistics Canada reported no growth in August GDP and an estimated decline in September, suggesting third-quarter growth may fall short of the Bank of Canada’s expectations following its latest interest rate increase. https://t.co/CCruoYeDlc — Canadian Mortgage Professional Magazine (@CMPmagazine) October 30, 2026

Development charges: OREA’s core demand

Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation (CMHC) data on how soaring development charges are reshaping Canada’s housing costs shows per-unit levies for a two-bedroom apartment ranging from approximately $39,600 in Ottawa to $121,500 in Markham, representing between 8% and 16% of new condo prices in parts of Ontario.

Kim Fairley, president of OREA, previously said the package delivers meaningful relief even for buyers well beyond Toronto.

“We’re talking homes up to $130,000 in a price difference,” Fairley said.

“That’s a big deal. Even for me up in Sault Ste. Marie — our new homes average between $600,000 and $700,000. Even for that spectrum, that’s a big difference for people up in the northern areas to have that swing into their favour when it comes to being able to buy that house.”

Brokers weigh in on ground-level impact

Despite OREA’s positive reception, concerns remain that development charge reform may fall short without coordinated municipal follow-through.

Matthew O’Neil of Connolly Capital in Toronto was candid about the pricing gap that continues to face first-time condo buyers.

“The problem with pre-con pricing is that even after this new rebate, it’s still priced way higher than resale,” O’Neil previously told Canadian Mortgage Professional.

“If you’re a first-time buyer and you want to buy a condo downtown, why would you buy preconstruction? It makes no sense. You’re looking at $1,300, $1,400, $1,500 a square foot — but you can go buy a resale condo for under $1,000 a square foot.”

OREA has specifically called for the HST rebate deadline to be pushed past March 31, 2027, to allow more families to access the measure.

Micky Khaneka of MKG Mortgages in Toronto told Canadian Mortgage Professional — amid ongoing questions around Ontario’s HST New Housing Rebate and how relief is applied at the point of sale — that the initiative still sends a clear market signal.

“I definitely think it’s a signal that the government’s listening and they’re really trying to reprioritize this because taking that out helps,” Khaneka said.
